label: Foundational beings possibly absent is an alternative to foundational beings necessary at w
note: Lane F (#2103). Same CausalityFrame, world w and FoundationalAt parameters. Target: the necessity verdict 666f06a4 (every foundational being at w exists at every accessible world). Mechanism: two verified routes conclude the rival verdict, that every foundational being at w is ContingentAt, i.e. exists at w and is absent at some accessible world. One route is existence-conditional essentialism (f9d43a47, result 872a3832): a foundational being's own essential truths hold at a representable point lacking it, and no other being's essential truth requires it. The other is Kant's thesis with concept adequacy (b08d83a2, result 63ac77e7). Justification: both are recorded positive accounts of modality through essence, with their premises open in the corpus, not a bare negation. They are not independent supports. Both routes use the essential-exclusion account 9d8a8d2e-23ff-4b74-8a06-6cd9abd7ccb8, which turns the absence of an existence-entailing essential truth into absence at some accessible world, and the unrequired-by-others premise 38200db5-a320-41c1-8eb6-ea4a6409ceb9. They differ only in how a foundational being's own essential truths are kept from entailing its existence. The first route uses existence-conditional essences (857654fe-e33b-4726-a7d8-8cb4b74791e2) with representable absence (d1af2b06-1ffe-41ff-ab3f-daa3305f8d44). The second uses Kant's thesis (9014eea0-3b72-4461-95b2-663490f72e4c) with concept adequacy (effbb158-308b-4d5c-a1b2-ee0b6048f321). Incompatibility: NecessaryAt requires existence at every accessible world and ContingentAt an accessible world lacking the being, so both verdicts together exclude any foundational being at w (c5da5e62, open). Without a foundational being both hold vacuously. Neither verdict is established; no refutation of the rival is recorded.
